package_info.why_malicious: These packages abuse the npm registry by storing and distributing large, non-software media files (such as pirated movies, videos, and eBooks) split into multiple parts. This violates npm's terms of service, threatens the integrity and availability of the registry, and enables illicit file hosting. The packages contain no functional software code and are designed solely for unauthorized media distribution, not legitimate development.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At package publish and install, the package delivers multiple large .ts video segment files by including them in the package root, resulting in the distribution of pirated or unauthorized media content to anyone who downloads or installs the package.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The presence of multiple large .ts files (video segments) in the root of an npm package is highly anomalous, as npm packages are expected to contain code or small, legitimate assets, not large media files.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages contain JavaScript/TypeScript code and small assets relevant to software development, not multi-gigabyte video content or media segments.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use might include small demo videos or sample assets for a media player library, but not full-length movies or large video files split into parts, especially without any code to utilize them.
key_indicators: Multiple large .ts files (video segments) present in package root
No JavaScript, TypeScript, or other executable code present
Package size (54.5 MB or more) far exceeds typical npm package sizes
File extensions and binary content unrelated to software development

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At package publish and install, the package delivers danmu.json files containing time-synced user comments (danmu) and playlist.m3u8 files as metadata, embedding them in subdirectories to accompany the pirated video content, resulting in the distribution of supporting data for unauthorized media playback.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: JSON files containing time-synced comments for video playback (danmu) and playlist.m3u8 streaming playlists are not expected in npm packages unless the package is a legitimate video player or similar tool. Here, they are used to support illicit media distribution without any code to process them.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages do not include large, structured comment data or streaming playlists for pirated media, especially in the absence of any code to utilize these files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use could occur in open-source video player projects with small demo data, but not in bulk-uploaded, non-functional packages containing only media and metadata.
key_indicators: danmu.json files with time-synced comment data in subdirectories
No code present to process or use these files
Files are directly associated with pirated media segments

attack_chain.action: Attacker splits pirated video content into multiple .ts files and prepares associated metadata files (danmu.json, playlist.m3u8) for each segment.
attack_chain.leads_to: Creation of large, non-software npm packages containing media segments and metadata.

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes hundreds of packages with the wlwz- prefix, each containing a segment of the pirated media and its associated metadata files.
attack_chain.leads_to: npm registry is flooded with non-software, media-hosting packages, increasing storage and bandwidth abuse.

attack_chain.action: Users or automated systems downloading these packages receive large video files and associated metadata instead of software, enabling unauthorized media distribution and registry abuse.
attack_chain.leads_to: Registry integrity and availability are threatened; potential for further abuse such as piracy, evasion of censorship, and undermining of supply chain trust.

behavioral_signatures: npm packages with no executable code and only large media files
Presence of multiple .ts files (video segments) in the package root directory
Inclusion of danmu.json and playlist.m3u8 files without any supporting code
Package size significantly exceeding typical npm packages (e.g., >50MB)
Package names matching the wlwz-* pattern and published in bulk
file_indicators: package.json with no main entry, scripts, or code fields
network_indicators: No network activity from the package itself, but detection of bulk downloads of large, non-code npm packages with wlwz-* names may indicate abuse
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Flag npm packages with the following characteristics: (1) package size greater than 50MB, (2) presence of multiple .ts files in the root directory, (3) inclusion of danmu.json or playlist.m3u8 files in any subdirectory, (4) absence of any JavaScript/TypeScript or other executable code, and (5) package names matching the wlwz-* pattern. Automated systems should alert or block such packages to prevent registry abuse and maintain supply chain hygiene. Monitor for bulk publishing or downloading of such packages as an additional indicator of abuse.
